transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

Well, I... I guess I'm here because things at work have just gotten really, really hard lately. I work in retail, you know, at this boutique downtown, and usually, I love it. I love arranging the displays and talking to people as they walk in. But recently, I just... I can't. I can't make myself go anywhere near the front windows. It's like my feet are glued to the floor if I even look in that direction. And it's not just the windows, it's that whole section of the street outside. If I have to walk past it to get to work, my heart starts racing, and I feel like I can't breathe, so I've been taking this ridiculously long detour just to use the back alley entrance. And once I'm inside, I just keep finding all these excuses to stay in the stockroom. I'll reorganize the same box of sweaters three times, or pretend I'm doing inventory, just so I don't have to go out onto the main floor near the glass. My manager is starting to get really annoyed because being out front is, like, half my job, but I just... I physically can't do it right now, and it's making everything a mess.
When you feel your heart racing and like you can't breathe before entering the front area, does this happen suddenly, and how long does it usually last?

I... gosh, I don't really know exactly how to time it, to be honest. It's really hard to pay attention to a clock when you feel like you're suffocating, you know? Like, I'll be walking to work, right? And maybe I'm totally fine when I get off the bus, just listening to a podcast or thinking about what I need to do that day, but as soon as I turn the corner and I know I'm getting closer to that part of the street... it just hits me. 

I don't know if you'd call that sudden, but it feels sudden to me because my chest just seizes up out of nowhere. And then my heart is just pounding, like, pounding so hard I can hear it in my ears while I'm rushing down that back alley detour I was telling you about. And it doesn't just stop the second I get through the back door, either. Even when I'm finally inside and I'm hiding out in the stockroom, I'll just be sitting there on this little step-stool we keep next to the shoe boxes, just trying to catch my breath. It feels like it takes absolutely forever for my heart to slow down. So I couldn't tell you if it's five minutes or twenty minutes or what. It just feels like this massive, exhausting ordeal every single morning, and I'm just completely drained before I even clock in.
Do you find yourself avoiding any other places or situations because you're worried about having these feelings again, where you might not be able to escape easily or get help if you need it?

I don't think so... I mean, it's really just that one specific area by the store, you know? Like, I'm totally fine going to the grocery store, or the coffee shop down the street from my apartment, or even just taking the bus. The bus is usually packed, and sometimes it gets stuck in traffic, which I guess is a situation where you can't really escape, but that doesn't bother me at all. I actually kind of like the bus because I can just put my headphones in and zone out. 

It's literally just that front section of the boutique and the street right outside it. If I'm anywhere else, I don't get that suffocating feeling or the racing heart. Even when I'm out with my friends on the weekends, we went to this really crowded movie theater last Saturday, and we were sitting right in the middle of the row where you have to awkwardly squeeze past like ten people if you need to go to the bathroom, and I didn't even think twice about it. I wasn't worried about being trapped or not getting help or anything like that. It's just... it's just work. Well, the front of work. The stockroom is fine. But yeah, nowhere else really makes me feel that way, just that one spot.
Have you ever experienced these same kinds of feelings — like your heart racing or trouble breathing — in any other specific situations, even if you weren’t near the store or avoiding something?

I don't think so, no. I mean, I've really been trying to think about it, because my mom was asking me something similar the other day when I called her. She was like, "Are you sure you're not just having panic attacks about everything?" and I had to tell her, no, mom, it's really not everything. It's just that one spot. 

Like, I've never had this happen before in my life. I've always been a pretty relaxed person, honestly. Even in high school, when we had to do those huge presentations in front of the whole class, you know, the ones where everyone else is sweating and shaking? I was totally fine. I'd just get up there and talk. I never got the racing heart or the feeling like I couldn't breathe. And I've never had it happen randomly, either. Like, I don't just wake up in the middle of the night feeling like that, and I don't get it when I'm just sitting on my couch watching TV or anything. 

It's literally just when I have to face that specific area by the store. If I'm not there, or if I'm not thinking about having to go there, I feel completely normal. My heart beats at a normal pace, I breathe totally fine. So, no, I haven't experienced it anywhere else or in any other situation. It's just... it's just that one place. It's so weird, isn't it? That your body can just react so strongly to one specific spot, but everywhere else is totally fine? I just don't understand it.
